scores.evidence: CD is asynchronous and pull-based: Argo CD reconciles from the config repo, so CI never holds prod credentials.
scores.rationale: Claims about GitHub Actions OIDC, keyless cosign, Kyverno admission audit/enforce modes, Argo HA/sharding, expand/contract migrations and GitOps semantics are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: Phase 4: Fleet onboarding (5 → 50) ... The whole organization is on one paved path, and the legacy pipelines are retired.
scores.rationale: Directly answers the sequencing request and is clearly buildable with explicit deferrals, but omits API/event contract-compatibility checking and test-data handling, implied core needs for 50 microservices.

scores.evidence: Consistency for deploy state. Git is the single source of truth for what runs where (GitOps).
scores.rationale: The GitOps consistency choice, role split, digest-only artifact model and tiered approvals are honored uniformly across every phase and table with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: A git revert in deploy-config rolls prod back, and that rollback has been demonstrated, not just assumed.
scores.rationale: Each phase has checkable exit criteria tied to its specific risks (broken release reverted within 5 minutes, DR restore drill, template rollback proven), with riskiest pieces validated first and DORA metrics continuing post-launch.

scores.evidence: Kubernetes, with one cluster per environment. This is stated as an assumption, not left silent.
scores.rationale: Every major decision has an explicit default plus a quantified revisit trigger describing what would change the design if the assumption proves wrong.

scores.evidence: A shared platform multiplies impact, so one bad template or one leaked credential can affect all 50 services.
scores.rationale: Covers the hardest domain failures — compromised templates, poisoned runners, platform-down hotfix paths, registry outage, drift, Git-host outage — each with concrete detection, containment and demonstrated recovery.

scores.evidence: An OTel span per pipeline stage. Argo metrics in Prometheus. Deploy annotations on Grafana. Alerts on sync or pipeline failure.
scores.rationale: Observability, safe rollback, migrations, break-glass, runbooks, DR drills and onboarding automation are designed in from day zero, with a buy-not-build burden plausible for a small platform team.

scores.evidence: Hosted CI minutes cost more than the total cost of running our own runners ... Then move to self-hosted ephemeral runners.
scores.rationale: The dominant driver (CI compute) is identified with concrete controls (autoscaling, concurrency limits, cost-per-pipeline reporting) and a build-vs-buy trade-off, but no order-of-magnitude estimate from expected build volume.

scores.evidence: A custom pipeline DSL or orchestrator. Not planned. Pull forward only if GitHub Actions reusable workflows provably can't express a pattern.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse commitments (artifact contract, service.yaml schema, repo topology, vendor coupling) are validated early with explicit exit and pull-forward paths, while reversible choices are decided quickly.

scores.evidence: Buy or adopt: GitHub Actions (CI), Argo CD (CD) ... Build only the glue: templates, the promotion policy, the service.yaml contract.
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest end-to-end slice, buys instead of building, defers Backstage, previews and hermetic builds with explicit triggers, and justifies the supply-chain machinery by the stated blast-radius constraint.

scores.evidence: If this is wrong, every later phase gets rewired, so it goes first.
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: concrete Phase 0 first steps, dependency-justified ordering, checkable exit criteria per phase, and revisit triggers that say how the plan adapts.

checklist.evidence: Each service declares owner, tier (1–3), archetype, build entrypoint, test entrypoint, health endpoint and whether it is stateful.
Pick 5 pilot services that cover at least 3 languages, plus one stateful service and one batch job.
Build once and promote the same immutable image digest through dev, staging and prod.
OIDC federation from CI to the cloud, with no static keys anywhere.
Every image gets an SBOM (Syft) and SLSA provenance. Every image is cosign-signed.
Expand/contract only, so the previous version still runs against the new schema.
Services with different shapes can onboard without writing platform code.
Build caching. Layer cache plus a dependency proxy or mirror. ... p95 commit-to-staging time is under 15 minutes.
Runner autoscaling with a minimum warm pool. Concurrency limits per repo.
Argo CD in HA mode ... Runbook for when the platform is down. ... Change-failure rate and MTTR are reported weekly.
A queryable deploy audit trail (who, which digest, when, which policy decision). ... Tier 1 needs two-person approval.

traps.evidence: Onboarding waves. Tier 3 first, then tier 2, then tier 1. ... Delete each old pipeline ... as each service cuts over.
Images are referenced by digest. Tags are informational only.
Service #1 is rebuilt using only OIDC, and every static CI secret has been deleted.
Capacity for 50 services × 3 environments (about 150 Argo apps).
A custom pipeline DSL or orchestrator. Not planned.

note: An exemplary, dependency-ordered plan that avoids every trap; only notable gaps are contract-compatibility testing, test-data handling, and quantified compute-cost estimates.
